title: Affine frames detect equality of section orientation maps
statement: In the setting of [def-trf-bundle-section-orientation-data], let N>0 annihilate finite A and be invertible on Noetherian S. Let f,g:L->B be arbitrary maps from the shifted finite Tate coefficient to the zero-section dualizing object. If for every affine open V and every rank-d linear frame e on V the inverse images of f and g become equal after postcomposition with the canonical bundleSectionChartComparison, then f=g.

proof.text: Finite Tate lines are flat. Induct on d using the single-flat-tensor and tensor/shift comparisons and the normalized Tate products to identify L with A_S(d)[2d].

The canonical unit purity map is invertible, so its zero-section pullback composed with the inverse coefficient comparison identifies L with B. Hence both objects have cohomology in the single degree -2d.

Refine local module frames by affine opens. The exceptional base-change mate in each frame is invertible by the open-base-change theorem, so cancel the chart comparison to get equality after ordinary restriction. The cohomology functor is injective on Hom between objects concentrated at -2d, and its restriction comparison is natural. The upper-star functors of the affine cover are jointly faithful on sheaves, proving equality of cohomology maps and hence f=g. Empty S uses the empty jointly surjective family.
